The sun hung low over the horizon, casting long shadows across the quiet street. A lone pigeon flapped its wings, searching for scraps of bread in the empty alley. The air smelled of rain and damp earth, a reminder that summer was fading into autumn.

I sat on the bench, watching the world pass by. A child laughed as she chased her shadow, while an old man adjusted his glasses and read a newspaper. Life moved on, indifferent to the small moments that made it beautiful.

I thought about the things I’d lost—dreams, time, the ability to feel things deeply. But then I remembered the warmth of a handshake, the taste of coffee on a cold morning, the way the wind whispered through the trees. Those were the things that mattered.

The pigeon landed on the bench beside me, tilting its head as if to say, *What are you thinking about?* I smiled and scratched its head. Maybe, just maybe, the world wasn’t so bleak after all.

The rain started to fall, soft at first, then harder, washing away the dust of the day. I stood up, my shoes splashing in the puddles, and walked home under the gray sky. Somewhere, a song played on a distant radio, and for a moment, the world felt a little less lonely.
